title: Two Sources
narrativeQuestion: What separated a rumor investigated by thousands from reporting by two people that helped end a presidency?

chapters.title: October 12, 1969
chapters.claim: A phone call to one trusted Detroit radio voice gave a rumor national transmission power.

chapters.title: October 14, 1969
chapters.claim: A Michigan Daily satire supplied most of the shared clue list after its original context fell away.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand People, One Source
chapters.claim: Apparent corroboration collapses when thousands of downstream checks trace to the same origins.

chapters.title: June 17, 1972
chapters.claim: A small burglary report became a presidential crisis only after twenty-six months of confirmation.

chapters.title: The Rule
chapters.claim: The Washington Post's two-independent-source rule traded speed for claims that could survive official attack.

chapters.title: What The Work Actually Was
chapters.claim: Records held facts steady and made later witness questions more exact.

namedPeople.name: Alexander Butterfield
namedPeople.role: White House staffer who confirmed the taping system

chapters.title: What Would Have Killed Each One
chapters.claim: A checkable claim names in advance what evidence would end it and allows that evidence to matter.

chapters.title: The Two Shapes
chapters.claim: Investigator count mattered less than a procedure that separated independent origins from repetition.

chapters.title: What The Unit Will Ask
chapters.claim: Trace origin, test independence, and name disproof before searching.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.claim: The terms board names evidence operations already performed in the story.

chapters.title: Note Repair
chapters.claim: The repair board corrects six durable misunderstandings about both investigations.

accuracyNotes: Describe national reach as about three weeks; accounts differ on the exact station-by-station spread.
State that Fred LaBour says he wrote satire and invented most of the famous clues; do not turn the page into a clue hunt.
Use November 7, 1969 for the Life issue only with the source note that exact cover dating should be checked against a scan before projection.
State the Washington Post standard as anonymous information requiring a second independent confirmation, while acknowledging formulations vary by account.
Do not reduce Watergate reporting to a garage informant; records, repeat interviews, editorial rules, hearings, and the tapes all matter.
Do not assign a single event or date to the rumor's end; it faded through loss of interest despite available disproof.
